title: AI How-To Video Maker for Your Products | AIVideosUGC
description: Use this AI how-to video maker to show your product in use, made from a single photo. Pick 9:16 for YouTube Shorts or 16:9 for your store page. Try it now.
h1: AI How-To Video Maker for Showing Products in Action
lead: Use this AI how-to video maker to show shoppers how your product works in 10, 15 or 30 seconds. Upload a photo, describe the task, and get a vertical or widescreen video for your store and YouTube Shorts.
intro: Here, your product gets used the way a customer would use it at home. The sample clip shows a woman running a handheld steamer down a creased blue shirt that hangs on a wooden clothes rack.

A quick how-to answers the question most shoppers have before they buy: how does this actually work? It suits tools and gadgets with one clear job, like garment steamers, milk frothers, lint shavers, or cleaning brushes. Put a 16:9 version on your product page and a 9:16 one on YouTube Shorts, then let the clip do the explaining.

A how-to product clip should teach one repeatable movement from a clear starting state to a visible result. A hand can switch on a steamer, press one pass across a shirt, and finish beside the smooth fabric. Keep the tool, the working surface, and the part being changed in frame so a shopper can understand what to do without guessing.

Write the steps in the order a customer would perform them: prepare the surface, use the tool once, and show the finished area. Mention the hand position, the pace, and the final hold. Add Step 1, Step 2, and Step 3 labels after download as editable layers, along with the product name and any safety instructions that come from your own documentation.

Review the tutorial at full-screen mobile size before publishing. Make sure the product is the same as the uploaded photo, the action is physically plausible, and the final result does not promise a measurement or performance you cannot support. Use the clip beside a listing or in a short feed ad where the first frame makes the problem and tool immediately clear.

A strong tutorial has one visible problem and one visible change. Begin with the wrinkled shirt, dry bristles, empty mug, or closed latch; show one deliberate movement; and hold on the finished state long enough for a shopper to compare it. Avoid a montage of unrelated features in a short clip.

Choose the destination before describing the frame. A [product video](/ai-video-generation/product-video) can sit beside a listing, a [YouTube Shorts ad](/platforms/youtube-shorts-ads) needs a vertical crop, and a [before-and-after video](/ai-video-generation/before-after-showcases) works when the changed surface is easy to see. The [Shopify product photo page](/platforms/shopify-product-photos) is useful when the lesson sits near a store listing.

For a sequence of product lessons, start with an [image-to-video clip](/ai-video-generation/image-to-video), then test a [UGC ad video](/ai-video-generation/ugc-ad-video) when a creator reaction adds context. The [first TikTok video ad guide](/guides/first-tiktok-video-ad), [product photo tips guide](/guides/product-photo-tips), and this how-to template help keep the source photo and final action aligned.
tip: Describe one task from start to finish, like "steams a wrinkled cotton shirt on a hanger, collar to hem," instead of listing every feature.

steps.t: Upload the product on its own

ideas.d: Show a milk frother foaming a latte or a garlic press working through a clove, one job per clip.

faq.q: Can one video show several steps in a row?
faq.a: Keep it to one clear task. At 10, 15 or 30 seconds, steaming a single shirt reads better than a full laundry routine. For a longer guide, make a few clips and join them in your editing app.

faq.q: Will the video include spoken instructions?
faq.a: AIVideosUGC does not add voiceover, music, or captions. Record your narration and add it with step text in your editor after download.

faq.q: Does the video have to match how my product really works?
faq.a: Yes. Describe the real way your product is used and watch the clip before you post it. If it shows something your product can't do, generate it again with a clearer description.

faq.q: How many steps fit in one tutorial?
faq.a: Keep it to one clear task with a starting state, the product action, and the finished state. Extra steps are easier to follow in a second clip.

faq.q: What length should a tutorial be?
faq.a: Ten seconds covers most single tasks; use 15 seconds for a slower demonstration, for 40 or 60 credits.

faq.q: Can viewers follow the steps when audio is unavailable?
faq.a: Add short step tags as a text layer after download, so the tutorial remains clear when the soundtrack is muted.

faq.q: Can I crop the tutorial to 1:1?
faq.a: Yes. Make a square version after download and check that the tool, hand, and finished result remain in frame.

faq.q: What product photo works best for a how-to video?
faq.a: Use a sharp photo that shows the entire tool and the part it touches, with no edge cropped out.

faq.q: How should I show a safety warning?
faq.a: Add the approved warning as editable step text after download and keep it beside the action it describes.

faq.q: Can I watch the tutorial with the sound off?
faq.a: Yes. Add short step labels after download so the sequence stays understandable when the soundtrack is muted.

overview.h2: Show one job from setup to result
overview.d: A useful how-to clip has a visible starting state, one product action, and a finished state. Ask for the hand position, the working surface, and the moment the task is complete so the scene explains the product without a spoken presenter.

overview.h2: Choose the frame for the place it will live
overview.d: Use 9:16 when the lesson will sit in a Shorts feed, 16:9 when it belongs beside a product description, 1:1 for a square feed, or 4:3 and 3:4 when another crop fits better. Make separate versions when the crop would hide the tool or the finished result.

input_guide.h2: Prepare a tool photo that can show the action

items.d: Photograph the nozzle, blade, whisk, brush, or handle in full so the requested movement has a clear reference.
For an item that opens, fills, clamps, or adjusts, include that part in its normal open position rather than hiding it in packaging.
A little space around the product gives a hand, fabric, cup, or counter room to enter the scene without covering the tool.
Say whether the action happens on a counter, hanger, sink, desk, or floor; one stable surface keeps the lesson readable.
The generated scene is strongest when one action carries the whole clip, such as steaming one shirt panel or frothing one mug.
Six, ten, fifteen, and thirty seconds use 24, 40, 60, and 120 credits; the exact cost is shown before you start.
The download gives you the moving product scene; add the step names, measurements, or instructions that must be exact.
A handheld steamer travels from cuff to shoulder on a hanging cotton shirt, ending on the smooth fabric.
A milk frother spins inside a clear mug on a breakfast counter, then lifts to reveal the foam.
A compact cleaning brush passes between keys on a desk beside the product box and a small pile of dust.
A hand closes the lid around prepared food on a kitchen table and presses the side latch once.

after_download.h2: Finish the lesson in your editor

items.d: Place short labels such as Fill, Press, and Rinse beside the matching moment.
Type capacity, temperature, or cleaning directions from your product information rather than relying on generated lettering.
Choose music or a voice track that matches the pace when the clip is ready for its channel.

good: Small appliances with a clear setup
Accessories that open, close, or adjust
not_ideal: Products whose value depends on several hidden steps
Claims that require a precise demonstration or measurement

steps.prompt: Use the uploaded photo as the product and keep its shape, color and label area exactly. Switch on this white handheld steamer beside a blue shirt, then press the fabric in one steady pass. Close side framing with one short push-in. Soft window light. End with the steamer beside the smooth panel of blue fabric. Sound: soft steam hiss and fabric movement; no music.

cards.label: Creator Demo: Electric toothbrush routine

In a clean bathroom, an adult lifts the electric toothbrush and brushes one front tooth section, ending with the brush lowered beside the sink. Natural morning-routine phone-video look, soft daylight. Mirror-level close framing with a slow push-in. Sound: toothbrush hum, faucet drip; no music.

cards.label: Creator Review: Headphones
cards.prompt: Use the uploaded photo as plain charcoal over-ear headphones and keep both ear cups visible. An adult presenter holds them at chest height in a bright living room while explaining the fit. Creator how-to product photo, square framing, no text or logos.

cards.label: Recipe Demo: Herbal tea steep
cards.prompt: Use the uploaded photo as the gooseneck kettle and keep its shape, finish, and control details. In a bright kitchen, an adult pours hot water over a tea bag in a clear mug, lets the tea steep, then lifts the mug to serve, showing the finished drink. Recipe-demo pacing, overhead-to-side close framing. Soft kitchen window light. End with the filled mug and kettle together, tea color clear. Sound: water pour and cup tap; no music.

cards.label: Before/After: Steamer smooths a shirt
cards.prompt: Use the uploaded photo as the garment steamer and preserve its shape and controls. An adult steams one wrinkled panel of a blue shirt in a smooth pass; end with the treated half visibly smooth beside the untouched wrinkles. Clear before-and-after product demo, close vertical framing. Soft window light. Sound: steam hiss and fabric rustle; no music.

cards.label: Creator Review: Field jacket fit check
cards.prompt: Use the uploaded photo as the field jacket and preserve its fabric and fit. An adult creator wears it, holds the cuff beside their face, looks directly into camera and says, “Watch how this cuff sits over my wrist.” Keep the face, moving mouth, and jacket visible in a chest-up handheld frame. Soft window light. End chest-up with the cuff near the lens and the field jacket collar clear. Sound: natural room tone; no music.

cards.label: Before/After: Grout brush cleans seam
cards.prompt: Use the uploaded photo as the product and keep its shape, color and label area exactly. In a tiled bathroom, an adult moves the grout brush once across a dirty seam, ending with the cleaned strip beside the untouched grout. Natural home-cleaning ad look, clear side light. Low close-up tracking the brush in one smooth move. Sound: brush bristles on tile, water drip; no music.

cards.label: Cooking Demo: Press garlic
cards.prompt: Use the uploaded photo as the product and keep its shape, color and label area exactly. At a bright kitchen counter, an adult places a peeled garlic clove in the press and squeezes once, ending with minced garlic on a board and the tool open. Natural food-prep phone-video look. Overhead handheld close-up with a short push-in. Soft kitchen window light. Sound: hinge squeeze, garlic on board; no music.
